children: Arabica coffee futures slid to a 10-week low on Thursday, weighed partly by a favourable outlook for next year's crop in top producer Brazil, while raw sugar prices rose to hit a 16-month peak.
settled down 3.9 cents, or 1.3%, at $2.8815 per lb, after setting a 10-week low of $2.8210.
* Dealers said this year's harvest in Brazil is now nearly complete and the focus was switching to prospects for the 2027 crop, which is off to a good start with ample rains favouring flowering.
* Exchange-certified stocks edged above a recent 26-year low, boosted by some additional supplies from Brazil, they also said.
* ICE arabica stocks stood at 220,452 bags as of September 9, up from 218,838 bags a day earlier. At the same time last year, stocks stood at 685,945 bags, dealers noted.
* There were also 54,310 bags from Brazil and 960 bags from Kenya pending grading.
​​settled up 0.33 cent, or 1.8%, at 18.73 cents per lb, after earlier hitting a 16-month high of 18.88 cents.
* Dealers said the run-up has been driven by tight supplies in top consumer India and the current strength of energy markets, which could encourage more use of cane to make the biofuel ethanol.

* The Indian government has asked sugar mills to ensure adequate supplies during the festival season, with domestic mills seeking to import nearly 800,000 tons of duty-free raw sugar, an official from the food ministry said on Thursday.

* Dealers noted September (LCCU6) was trading at a discount of around £200 to December (LCCZ6) in the run-up to its expiry on September 15, indicating little appetite to take delivery of cocoa against the contract.
* Nestle said it is boosting its cocoa buying in Brazil, as it tries to diversify sourcing.
